rationale: Malachi says the reverent will belong to God on the day of His acquisition. Exodus promises that those hearing His voice and keeping His covenant will be His treasured people among the nations, expressing the same claim of belonging to God.
source_text: “They will be Mine,” says the Lord Almighty, “for a day that I am making for an acquisition, and I will choose them as a man chooses his son who serves him.

target_units.text: Now therefore, if you diligently listen to My voice, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the sons of Israel.”

rationale: Malachi promises a visible distinction between righteous and lawless people and between serving God and not serving. Matthew portrays final separation in which service or failure to serve the needy is addressed as service or failure toward the King, ending in different outcomes for the righteous and the others.
source_text: And you will return and see the distinction between the righteous and the lawless, and between one who serves God and one who does not serve.

target_units.text: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.
All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.
Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,
naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’
Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?
When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?
When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,
I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’
Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’
And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

rationale: Malachi compares the lawless to straw burned on the coming day, leaving neither root nor branch. Isaiah likewise describes a stalk consumed by flame and roots becoming chaff because the people rejected the Lord's law.
source_text: For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.

target_units.text: Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.

The Lord Sabaoth was enraged with wrath against His people, brought His hand against them and struck them. The mountains were roused, and their carcasses became like dung in the middle of the road. In all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.

rationale: Malachi describes the lawless as straw ignited by the coming day. Obadiah depicts Jacob and Joseph as fire and flame consuming Esau as stubble, using the same image of combustible plant matter for those under judgment.
source_text: For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.

target_units.text: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

rationale: Malachi promises the rising sun of righteousness with healing for those who fear God's name. Zechariah's prophecy in Luke describes a visiting dawn from above that shines on those in darkness and directs them into peace; both portray divine deliverance through rising light.
source_text: But for you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; you will go out and leap like little calves released from bonds.

target_units.text: through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine upon those who sit in darkness and death’s shadow, to direct our feet into a way of peace.”

rationale: Malachi's rising sun brings healing and release for the reverent. Isaiah calls Jerusalem to shine because the Lord's glory has risen upon her despite surrounding darkness, with nations walking by that light. The connection is the restorative light image, not an assertion that every detail is identical.
source_text: But for you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; you will go out and leap like little calves released from bonds.

target_units.text: Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the Lord’s glory has risen upon you.
Behold, darkness and gloom will cover earth over nations, but the Lord will appear upon you, and His glory will be seen over you.
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.

rationale: Malachi promises that the lawless will be ashes under the feet of the addressed people. Isaiah describes God bringing high fortified cities to the ground to be trampled by the feet of the meek and lowly, similarly placing the judged power beneath the feet of those God vindicates.
source_text: You will trample the lawless, because they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day that I am making,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Thou who didst humble and bring down those dwelling on high. Thou wilt cast down fortified cities and bring them to the ground,
and the feet of the meek and lowly will trample them.

rationale: Malachi promises Elijah before the Lord's day. Matthew records the expectation that Elijah must come first and Jesus' explanation that Elijah has already come, which the disciples understand as referring to John the Baptist.
source_text: “And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,

target_units.text: The disciples asked Him, “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered, “Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things.
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. In the same way the Son of Man is also to suffer at their hands.”
Then the disciples understood that He spoke to them about John the Baptist.

rationale: Malachi announces Elijah before the coming divine day. Luke describes John going before the Lord in Elijah's spirit and power to prepare a ready people, applying Elijah's preparatory role while naming John as the child in context.
source_text: “And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,

target_units.text: He will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

He himself will go before Him in Elijah’s spirit and power, to turn fathers’ hearts toward children and the disobedient to the understanding of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.”

rationale: Malachi assigns Elijah a future preparatory mission before the Lord's great day. Sirach's praise of Elijah recalls his fiery departure and his recorded appointment to still anger before wrath and restore Jacob's tribes, a corresponding description of his appointed role.
source_text: “And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,

target_units.text: You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with fiery horses.
You were recorded in rebukes for appointed times: to still anger before wrath, to turn a father’s heart toward a son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

rationale: Malachi says the promised Elijah will restore a father's heart toward a son and a person's heart toward a neighbor. Luke echoes the fathers-to-children restoration in describing John in Elijah's spirit, while giving its further clause as turning the disobedient toward righteous understanding.

rationale: Both texts assign Elijah the turning of a father's heart toward a son before threatened wrath. Sirach adds restoration of Jacob's tribes, while Malachi's further wording concerns a person's heart toward a neighbor; the shared paternal phrase is retained without merging those clauses.

rationale: Malachi closes by commanding remembrance of Moses' law, ordinances and judgments given at Horeb for Israel. Deuteronomy warns against forgetting the Horeb encounter and recounts the command to teach its ordinances and judgments to the people and their children.
source_text: “All of you, remember the law of Moses My servant, as I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, ordinances and judgments.”

target_units.text: Take heed unto yourself, and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget all the things which your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. And you shall teach your sons and your sons’ sons

the day when you stood before the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, when the Lord said unto me: Assemble the people unto Me, and let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live upon the earth, and may teach their sons.
And you drew near and stood beneath the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire unto heaven, with darkness, gloom, tempest, and a great sound.
And the Lord spoke unto you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but saw no likeness, only a voice.
And He declared unto you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, even the ten words; and He wrote them upon two tablets of stone.
And the Lord commanded me at that time to teach you ordinances and judgments, that you should do them in the land whither you go to inherit it.
